title: Best CRO tools for B2B websites
summary: The best CRO tools for B2B websites, split into page tools and conversation tools, with prices and the traffic you need to A/B test. By Storylane.
body_markdown:
Ask a B2B demand gen team how they run conversion rate optimization and most will describe an A/B testing program. Then ask how many tests reached a clear result last quarter. The tools work. The problem is that most B2B pages never get enough visitors for a test to say anything, and most visitors who leave were not put off by the button but by a question the page could not answer.


So I sort CRO tools into two groups. **Page tools** watch and test the page: analytics, heatmaps, A/B testing and personalization. **Conversation tools** respond to the buyer: smarter forms, interactive demos and website agents. B2B sites need both, but with modest traffic, the second group holds most of the pipeline.


I work at Storylane, and two of the tools below are ours. Every tool gets a fair "pick it if", and prices come from each vendor's own site, checked November 12, 2026.

## Why can't most B2B websites A/B test their way to more pipeline?


Because a test needs a lot of visitors to see a small change, and B2B pages rarely have them. I call this the **traffic floor** : the number of visitors a page needs before an A/B test can tell a real lift from noise.


An illustrative example with standard test settings (95% confidence, 80% power). Say your demo request page converts 2% of visitors and you want to detect a 20% relative lift, from 2.0% to 2.4%. You need about 21,100 visitors per version, roughly 42,200 in total. At 5,000 visitors a month, that test runs for more than eight months. If you only care about a 50% lift, the total drops to about 7,600 visitors, or six weeks. But lifts that big are rare and hard to predict.


Personalization makes the floor higher, not lower. Split traffic into five industries and each segment gets a fifth of the visitors and needs its own test. Our guide to[website personalization tools](https://www.storylane.io/blog/website-personalization-tools) covers that tradeoff.


The fair objection: test a higher-volume step, like hero button clicks. That is the right move if you test at all. But a click is not a meeting. A win on clicks that does not show up in demos booked is a[B2B conversion rate optimization](https://www.storylane.io/blog/b2b-conversion-rate-optimization) result that looks good in a deck and nowhere else.


## What do B2B buyers leave the website without?


Answers, mostly. The[Storylane Buyability Index](https://buyability-index.storylane.io/) generated 10,580 buyer questions for 529 B2B websites and checked whether each site answered them. Only 58.6% got a full answer, and pricing questions were fully answered 46.4% of the time. (The questions were generated per company as what a buyer would plausibly ask, not logged from real buyers; the 529 sites were hand-picked and scanned between September 8 and October 20, 2026.)


When a site does answer, it often[sits in the docs, not on the page the buyer landed on](https://www.storylane.io/blog/website-answers-hidden-in-docs) . And price is the question buyers want first:[Storylane's Modern Buying Trends 2026 report](https://www.storylane.io/buyer-experience-report) found that pricing opens 9.4% of website agent conversations, against 2.5% of sales calls. So[put pricing on your website](https://www.storylane.io/blog/should-you-put-pricing-on-your-website) before you test the button under it.


That is why page tools hit a ceiling. A test can change the headline, layout or button, but not make the page answer a question it does not know the buyer has. **A/B testing optimizes what the page says; most B2B visitors leave over what it doesn't say.**


## Conversation tools: respond to the buyer


### Storylane RepX


[Storylane RepX](https://www.storylane.io/repx) is a website agent. It answers buyer questions in text, voice or video, shows interactive demos mid-conversation (see[how an agent runs the demo in conversation](https://www.storylane.io/blog/ai-agent-demo-in-conversation) ) when each demo's plain-language[display instruction](https://docs.storylane.io/repx-chat/training-repx/demos-images-and-videos) fits, qualifies visitors on your ICP, handles objections like pricing pushback and competitor comparisons, and books the meeting.[Playbooks](https://docs.storylane.io/repx-chat/playbooks/introduction-to-playbooks) set starter questions, intro message, CTA buttons, qualification questions and meeting link per page, so the pricing page can book an AE while the docs page books support. Each Playbook also sets[when RepX asks for an email](https://docs.storylane.io/repx-chat/playbooks/qualification-behavior-and-goals) : work emails only, after a set number of messages, or once the visitor qualifies.[Storylane's Modern Buying Trends 2026 report](https://www.storylane.io/buyer-experience-report) found that 1% of buyers share an email after one message and 31% after five or six, the case for[converting visitors without forms](https://www.storylane.io/blog/convert-visitors-without-forms) . Guardrails set rules on pricing, competitors and compliance, and evaluations let you[test the agent](https://docs.storylane.io/repx-chat/setting-up-repx/testing-your-agent) before launch. For CRO teams, the[launch options](https://docs.storylane.io/repx-chat/setting-up-repx/launching-on-your-website) matter most: a chat widget or immersive view, a dedicated RepX page, or a conversation that starts after a conversion goal such as a demo form submit.[JavaScript functions](https://docs.storylane.io/repx-chat/advanced/javascript-functions) open RepX from your own button, so a hero CTA can start a conversation instead of a form. Qualified leads and conversation summaries flow to HubSpot, Salesforce and Slack.


It is best for demand gen teams and webmasters who want more of their existing traffic to become pipeline. It goes straight at the answer gap above and works at any traffic level, because it needs no test to reach significance before it helps the next visitor.[Storylane's Modern Buying Trends 2026 report](https://www.storylane.io/buyer-experience-report) found that 51.4% of conversations with website agents start outside the buyer's working hours (8,211 conversations across 19 companies, in the buyer's local time), when no test and no rep is helping. Hospitable booked[36 meetings and 7 closed-won deals in RepX's first month](https://www.storylane.io/customer-stories/how-hospitable-booked-36-meetings-in-a-month-with-repx) . RepX starts at $2,000 a month, and the price depends on website traffic.


### Storylane Demo Suite


Demo Suite lets buyers click through your product on the website. It is best for teams whose buyers want to see the product before a call, often with rivals open in other tabs. It answers the question no headline test can: "what does this actually look like?" Growth adds A/B testing of the demos themselves (see[A/B testing demo variants](https://www.storylane.io/blog/ab-testing-demo-variants) ). There is a free plan, and paid plans run $50, $625 and $1,500 a month billed monthly, with Enterprise on request ([storylane.io/plans](https://www.storylane.io/plans) ). For numbers on how demos convert, see our[interactive demo conversion benchmarks](https://www.storylane.io/blog/interactive-demo-conversion-benchmarks) , and for where to put them,[CRO best practices for SaaS demo pages](https://www.storylane.io/blog/cro-best-practices-demo-pages) .


### Chili Piper


Chili Piper turns a form fill into a booked meeting before the buyer leaves the page, routing each lead to the right rep. Growth starts at $1,250 a month with 15 seats included, and Scale at $3,500 a month. It fixes a real leak: the gap between "I filled in the form" and "someone called me back", which is why[speed to lead](https://www.storylane.io/blog/what-is-speed-to-lead) matters. It helps buyers already ready to talk. **Pick Chili Piper if** plenty of people fill in your form but too few reach a meeting. Our post on[why contact forms suppress conversion](https://www.storylane.io/blog/why-contact-forms-suppress-conversion) covers when the form itself is the problem.


## Page tools: watch and test the page


### Microsoft Clarity


Clarity records sessions and builds heatmaps of clicks, scrolls and drop-offs. Its site says it is "Free forever" with "No limits on traffic", and it adds AI summaries and AI citation tracking. Like every analytics tool, it shows where people stopped, not what they wanted. **Pick Clarity if** you have no behavior analytics today. Install it first; it is free and shows which pages deserve the rest of this list.


### Contentsquare (formerly Hotjar)


Hotjar's site now says "Hotjar is now Contentsquare". The free plan covers up to 200,000 sessions a month with replays, heatmaps, funnels and basic surveys. Growth is from $39 a month billed annually ($49 monthly), with Pro and Enterprise quote-based. For B2B, the on-page surveys are the useful part: visitors can tell you what was missing. **Pick Contentsquare if** you want analytics and a simple way to ask visitors questions in one place.


### VWO


VWO's site, now at wingify.com, says "VWO and AB Tasty have come together". It covers website experimentation "built for non-technical teams", heatmaps and recordings, and real-time personalization. Plans are quote-based, with a 30-day free trial. The traffic floor applies in full, so it suits pages with volume. **Pick VWO if** a marketer, not an engineer, will run your tests and your key pages clear the traffic floor.


### Optimizely


Optimizely sells experimentation (A/B, multi-page, feature and server-side tests), personalization and a CMS. Its pricing page says "Every Optimizely plan is individually packaged", so it is quote-based. **Pick Optimizely if** you run high-traffic web and product experiments and want one platform for both.


## Which CRO tools should a B2B team start with?


Start from your traffic, not from the tool list.


- **Below the traffic floor** (most B2B pages): install Clarity or Contentsquare to see behavior, then spend on conversation tools: interactive demos to show the product and a website agent to answer questions.
- **Above the traffic floor** on a few pages: add VWO or Optimizely for those pages only, and measure tests on meetings booked, not clicks.
- **Leads stall after the form:** fix routing and scheduling with Chili Piper before you test anything upstream.


The[agentic inbound conversion playbook](https://www.storylane.io/blog/agentic-inbound-conversion) covers how the conversation side fits the rest of inbound.


The idea to keep is the traffic floor. Before you plan a test, work out how many visitors it needs. If the answer is more than your page gets in a quarter, stop testing that page and answer the buyer instead.
